TimePeriod: From Genesis through the prophets (Arabian nomad horizon)
Region: The Arabian desert east of Israel, in tents and villages (Isaiah 42:11; Psalm 120:5)
History: Kedar, son of Ishmael, heads the Arabian nomads of the prophets. Psalm 120:5 makes 'the tents of Kedar' proverbial for distant dwelling, and the Song of Songs borrows the same image for dark tents (Song of Songs 1:5). Isaiah 21:16-17 gives Kedar's glory a single year to fail, Isaiah 42:11 calls the villages that Kedar inhabits to sing, Isaiah 60:7 gathers 'the flocks of Kedar' to the restored Zion, Jeremiah 49:28 sends Nebuchadnezzar against Kedar's men of the east, and Ezekiel 27:21 has Arabia and the princes of Kedar trading lambs, rams, and goats with Tyre.
Culture: Nomadic herders of the Arabian desert, living in tents and villages, trading flocks with Tyre.
Religion: Nothing distinct is recorded of Kedarite religion.
BibleConnection: Kedar is the desert neighbor in Israel's poetry and prophecy: the psalmist's distant tent, Isaiah's doomed glory and gathered flock, Jeremiah's target.
KeyScriptures: Genesis 25:13; Psalm 120:5; Isaiah 21:16; Isaiah 42:11; Isaiah 60:7; Jeremiah 49:28; Ezekiel 27:21
